questions.question: Plants that do not have well - differentiated body design fall in this group. The plants in this group are commonly called algae. This group is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thallophytes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thallophytes**:-

 
 
• **These are a diverse group of organisms that includes both unicellular and multicellular plants. **
 
• They are found in a wide range of habitats, from freshwater and marine environments to terrestrial environments.
 
• Thallophytes do not have true roots, stems, or leaves. Instead, their bodies are typically flattened and leaf-like, and they absorb water and nutrients directly from their environment.
 
• **The group of plants that do not have a well-differentiated body design and are commonly called algae is thallophyta.**
 
• Examples of thallophytes include:
 
 
• **Green algae:** Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora
 
• **Brown algae**: Fucus, Laminaria, Sargassum
 
• **Red algae**: Porphyra, Gelidium, Gracilaria
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gymnosperms:-

 
 
• These are a group of plants that produce seeds but do not have flowers. 
 
• They include conifers, cycads, ginkgoes, and others.
 
• Gymnosperms have a higher number of species compared to bryophytes and algae.
 
• Gymnosperms are typically slow in terms of reproduction; up to a year may pass between pollination and fertilisation and seed maturation may require 3 years.
 
 
 
• **Bryophytes**:-
 
 
• **These are a group of non-vascular plants that includes mosses, liverworts, and hornworts. **
 
• They are called non-vascular plants because they do not have specialized tissues for transporting water and nutrients, such as xylem and phloem.
 
• Bryophytes are typically small plants that grow in moist, shady environments. They are found all over the world, from the Arctic to the tropics.
 
 
 
• **Pteridophytes**:-
 
 
• **These are vascular plants that reproduce by spores. **
 
• They are also known as ferns and lycophytes.
 
• Pteridophytes were the first vascular plants to colonize the land, and they played a major role in the evolution of plant life.

questions.question: Identify the place in India where tropical cyclones originate from.

options.text: Bay of Bengal and Indian ocean

• **Most tropical cyclones in India originate from the Bay of Bengal and Indian ocean.**
 
• **Bay of Bengal:-**
 
 
• The Bay of Bengal is a large body of warm water that is located to the east of India.
 
• The warm water provides the energy that tropical cyclones need to form and intensify.
 
 
 
• **Indian Ocean:-**
 
 
• **The Indian Ocean is the third-largest of the world's five oceanic divisions, covering 70,560,000 km2 (27,240,000 sq mi) or ~19.8% of the water on Earth's surface. **
 
• It is bounded by Asia to the north, Africa to the west and Australia to the east. To the south it is bounded by the Southern Ocean or Antarctica depending on the definition in use.
 
• Along its core, the Indian Ocean has some large marginal or regional seas such as the Arabian Sea, Laccadive Sea, Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea.

questions.question: Which among the following waves is not an electromagnetic wave?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cathode Rays.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Cathode Rays:-**

 
 
• **Cathode rays are streams of electrons emitted from the cathode (negatively charged electrode) of a vacuum tube. **
 
• They are produced when a high voltage is applied between the cathode and another electrode, called the anode (positively charged electrode).
 
• The electrons are accelerated by the electric field and travel through the vacuum tube at high speeds.
 
• **It is not an Electronic Magnetic Wave.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ultraviolet (UV) rays:-**

 
 
• **These are a type of electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths shorter than visible light and longer than X-rays. **
 
• UV rays are not visible to the human eye, but they can have a significant impact on our health and the environment.
 
• UV rays are produced by the sun, but they can also be produced by artificial sources, such as tanning beds and germicidal lamps.
 
 
 
• **Infrared (IR) rays:-**
 
 
• **These are a type of electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths longer than visible light and shorter than microwaves. **
 
• IR rays are not visible to the human eye, but we can feel them as heat.
 
• IR rays are produced by all objects with a temperature above absolute zero. The hotter the object, the more IR rays it produces.
 
 
 
• **Gamma rays:**
 
 
• **These are the most energetic type of electromagnetic radiation. **
 
• They have shorter wavelengths and higher energies than X-rays.
 
• Gamma rays are produced by radioactive decay, nuclear reactions, and certain astronomical events.
 
• Gamma rays are highly penetrating and can damage living cells. They are used in a variety of applications, such as cancer treatment, medical imaging, and materials science.

questions.question: Which of the following Satyagraha was led by Dr. B R Ambedkar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahad Satyagraha.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Mahad Satyagraha:-**

 
 
• **The Mahad Satyagraha was a non-violent protest movement led by B. R. Ambedkar on March 20, 1927.**
 
• It's aim was to assert the rights of untouchables to use water in a public tank in Mahad, Maharashtra, India.
 
• The day (20 March) is observed as Social Empowerment day in India.
 
• The upper-caste Hindus in Mahad were enraged by the Mahad Satyagraha. They attacked the satyagrahis with stones and sticks.
 
• Ambedkar himself was injured in the attack. The satyagrahis were forced to retreat, but they had made their point.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Individual Satyagraha:-**

 
 
• **It was the outcome of the August Offer. **
 
• The movement started not only for independence but also for freedom of speech.
 
• Vinoba Bhave was the 1st Satyagrahi and J.L.Nehru and Brahma Dutt were the 2nd and 3rd one.
 
• It started in Oct 1940 and lasted till Dec 1941. The movement created little enthusiasm and thus, Gandhiji suspended it.
 
 
 
• **Kanpur Satyagraha;-**
 
 
• **It was a non-violent protest movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi in April 1922 in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, India. **
 
• The movement was a protest against the British government's decision to establish a cloth market reserve in the city.
 
• The reserve would have forced Indian merchants to move to a less desirable location, which would have hurt their businesses.
 
 
 
• **Kheda Satyagraha:-**
 
 
• **It was a non-violent protest movement led by Mahatma Gandhi and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in 1918 in Kheda district of Gujarat, India. **
 
• The movement was a protest against the British government's decision to increase the land revenue in the district, even though the farmers had suffered a severe drought in 1917.

questions.question: Hymns of the Rigveda are known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sukta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rigveda**

 
 
• **It is an ancient Indian collection of Vedic Sanskrit hymns.**
 
• It is the oldest known Vedic Sanskrit text.
 
• It is one of the four sacred canonical texts of Hinduism.
 
• **It contains 1028 hymns which are arranged in 10 mandalas.**
 
• The sum of the hymns in Rigveda is in the form of Dialogue.
 
• **Hymns of the Rigveda are known as Sukta.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Adhyay**:-

 
 
• **It means "chapter" or "section". It is used to refer to the divisions of the Rigveda, which is divided into ten books (maṇḍalas), each of which is further divided into hymns (sūktas). **
 
• The hymns are then further divided into verses (ṛcas).
 
 
 
• **Yami**:-
 
 
• **It is the twin sister of Yama, the god of death. **
 
• She is mentioned in several hymns of the Rigveda, including the famous Yama-Yami hymn (RV 10.10).
 
 
 
• **Shudra**:-
 
 
• **It means "servant" or "worker". In the Rigveda, the Shudras are the lowest social class. **
 
• They are often associated with manual labor and are considered to be inferior to the other three social classes: the Brahmins (priests and scholars), the Kshatriyas (warriors and rulers), and the Vaishyas (merchants and farmers).

questions.question: In which year the planning commission was set up in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1950**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Planning Commission-**

 
 
• The **Planning Commission of India** was established on the year **15th March 1950**.
 
• The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairman of this Commission.
 
• There is** no provision for (or mention of) the Planning Commission in the Constitution of India**.
 
• It was constituted in the form of an advisory and specialist institution.
 
• It was constituted by the Union Cabinet on the proposal of a member of the Union Parliament.
 
• The government has changed its organization and structure from time to time.
 
• **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Chairman of the Planning Commission.**
 
• There is no fixed term/tenure of the Deputy Chairman and members of the Planning Commission.
 
• The commission estimates the physical capital and the human resources commission prepare plans for maximum effective and impartial use of national resources.
 
• The commission makes a critical analysis of each step and gives reformative suggestions.
 
• Final clearance to planning is given by the “National Development Council”.
 
• **1st national planning committee** was set up in **1938 by Subhash Chandra Bose and chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India)**

 
 
• NITI Aayog Replaces Planning Commission in** 2015 **after 65 years by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• NITI Aayog is not a constitutional body. It is an executive body.
 
• It was established on** January 1, 2015**.
 
• The ex-officio president of this is the Prime Minister.
 
• It is the premier policy ‘Think Tank’ of the Government of India, providing both directional and policy inputs.

• The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) is a government of India scheme launched on July 15, 2015.
 
• **It provides skill training to unemployed youth and working professionals. The scheme aims to train 40 million people by 2022.**
 
• **It is a flagship scheme of the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship.**
 
• The PMKVY is a demand-driven scheme, meaning that the courses offered are aligned with the needs of the industry.
 
• The scheme offers a wide range of courses, from short-term courses of 3 to 6 months to longer courses of 1 year or more.
 
• The PMKVY is open to all unemployed youth and working professionals who are at least 18 years old. There are no educational qualifications required to apply for the scheme.

__
 
• The First Five Year Plan of India was based on the Harrod Domar Model.
 
• First Five-Year Plan of India:
 
 
• It was launched for the duration of 1951 to 1956, under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• It was based on the Harrod-Domar model with a few modifications.
 
• Its main focus was on the agricultural development of the country.
 
• This plan was successful and achieved a growth rate of 3.6% (more than its target of 2.1%). 
 
• At the end of this plan, five IITs were set up in the country.

Second Five-Year Plan (1956‑61):

 
 
• This plan was based on the P.C. Mahalanobis Model.

questions.question: In India, who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Chief Election Commissioner:**

__
 
• The President appoints Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners.
 
• They have a fixed tenure of six years, or up to the age of 65 years.
 
• The commission consists of one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.
 
• Chief Election Commissioner enjoys the same status and receives salary and perks as available to Judges of the Supreme Court of India.​
 
• **Procedure for Removal:**​
 
 
• Chief Election Commissioner may be removed from office through a motion adopted by Parliament on grounds of ‘Proven misbehavior or incapacity.
 
• Removal requires a special majority of 2/3rd members present and voting.
 
• It should be supported by more than 50% of the total strength of the house.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Vice President of India:-**

 
 
• **He is the second-highest constitutional office in the country, after the President. **
 
• The Vice President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of both houses of Parliament, the Rajya Sabha (upper house) and the Lok Sabha (lower house).
 
• The Vice President holds office for a term of five years and can be re-elected.
 
 
 
• **Speaker of the Lok Sabha:-**
 
 
• **He is the presiding officer and the highest authority of the Lok Sabha, the lower house of the Parliament of India. **
 
• The Speaker is elected generally in the first meeting of the Lok Sabha following general elections. Serving for a term of five years, the Speaker is chosen from sitting members of the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister of India:-**
 
 
• **It is the head of the government of the Republic of India. **
 
• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President of India and must maintain the confidence of the Lok Sabha (lower house of Parliament).
 
• The Prime Minister holds office at the pleasure of the President and can be removed from office if he or she loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
